title: Contextual Column Compression and Density Snapshot for Virtual Tables
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our virtualized table has grown multiple one-off behaviors: hard column compression modes, an all-or-nothing compact density toggle, and a heavy-handed resize affordance that makes column prioritization opaque. This causes inconsistent UX across Console routes and makes it difficult for product teams to tune density vs readability without engineering changes.

Goal: Introduce a contextual column compression model and a density snapshot control that lets users (and the Console) predictably trade horizontal space for information density without breaking virtualization heuristics or KV caching. Provide clear affordances for which columns are compressible, which should snap to min-widths, and how sort/filter chips behave when columns collapse.

Scope: This ticket owns the interaction design, token guidance, and edge-case patterns required for implementation teams. Engineering work (runtime batching or virtualization internals) will be in ENG tasks; this ticket surfaces acceptance criteria, interaction specs, accessibility requirements, and measurement signals.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle a new Density Snapshot control (Compact / Balanced / Spacious) at the table header and see deterministic column layout changes without rehydrating the entire table.
A visual affordance (compressible chevron) appears on columns that are eligible for compression; it persists across horizontal scroll and is discoverable by keyboard focus.
Column resize interaction supports a soft-compress drag: dragging past a threshold enters compressed state (snap animation) and emits a telemetry event.
Sorting and filtering UI adapts to column compression: when a column compresses, its filter chip collapses to an icon with tooltip; sort order remains visible via a condensed chip.
All interactions meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and keyboard operability; screen readers expose density mode and which columns are compressed.
Design tokens for min/max widths, compression breakpoints, and density spacing are documented and mapped to existing density token scale (density-0..density-4).
implementation_notes: The runtime must expose a stable per-column 'compressibility' flag so virtualization can reserve KV cache lengths and avoid layout thrash.
Column min-widths should be expressed as tokens (token names in doc) to allow runtime mapping for quantized model variants (e.g., narrow-mode for mobile).
Provide CSS-only fallback for non-JS routes: density snapshot maps to a utility class (rs-density-compact / balanced / spacious).
When a column is in compressed state, persist an analytics attribute data-col-compressed=true on DOM cell elements for easier instrumentation.
comments: 2026-02-12 - MP: Initial sketch uploaded to Figma, called out three density tiers and proposed microcopy for the header control.
2026-02-20 - AC: Feasibility sync with ENG; virtualization runtime requires a compressibility hint. ENG suggested a fallback where the client estimates width from first N rows.
2026-02-26 - PM (Jordan Li): Product likes density snapshot but requests an A/B friendly flag to measure downstream metrics (time-to-find, average column width).
2026-03-03 - Accessibility review (Priya Rao): Suggested accessible names for the compressible chevron and recommended a visible focus ring and ARIA-expanded when a column is fully collapsed.
2026-03-10 - AC: Updated interaction to include soft-compress threshold and added telemetry events list to Implementation Notes. Ready for design review with stakeholders.
accessibility_considerations: Compressible affordance must be keyboard reachable (tab index) and actionable via Enter/Space.
Provide an ARIA region announcing 'Density changed to Compact/Balanced/Spacious' to reduce cognitive load when the entire table relayouts.
When filter chips collapse to icons, an offscreen label should be present so screen reader users can understand state and open the filter panel.
Avoid relying on color alone for compression state; use iconography + textual tooltip for low-vision users.
telemetry_goals: Record density_mode_changed with previous_mode and new_mode.
Emit column_compress_toggled events with column_key and method (drag / header-toggle / density-snapshot).
Track downstream metrics: average columns visible per viewport, average row height, and time-to-action (clicks) on compact vs spacious modes for top 3 Console routes.
qa_checklist: Verify density snapshot persists across page reloads and route navigation when user has persisted preferences enabled.
Confirm keyboard-only users can compress/uncompress columns and switch density modes without pointer input.
Check virtualization stability when many columns compress/uncompress rapidly (no row jitter, no lost focus).
Validate token mapping: min-width tokens apply correctly across themes and breakpoints.
Ensure telemetry events are emitted with required attributes and show in staging analytics dashboard.
